gates.evidence: The news app content provided is standard general and entertainment news, and the proposal focuses on clearing advertisements, which is SFW.
The reward is an in-app ad-free status; there is no incentive to click ads or install third-party apps.
The proposal uses gain framing (ad-free time) rather than threatening content loss or account deletion.
The proposal includes an offer card with a clear 'Start Sprint' button and an opt-out path.
The offer card clearly states: 'Play a 15-second game with our News Anchor to remove all feed and article advertisements.'
The offer card includes a 'No thanks' button which dismisses the prompt without penalty.
The offer is placed in the feed (s02) after top stories, not mid-article or during interactive elements.
The proposal limits eligibility to 'Non-signed-in users currently viewing high-density native and banner advertisements.'

scores.evidence: The proposal triggers during browsing (s02) where ad density is high, matching the user's need for a clean reading experience.
Clearing ads from a news feed preserves content; the in-world 'News Anchor' interaction feels appropriate for a news app.
15-minute bursts are sampling-oriented and limited (3/day), which unlikely cannibalizes long-term subscriptions.
Granting 15 minutes of ad-free time has zero COGS and provides revenue through the 15-second rewarded play, consistent with the economics provided.
The trigger is on the Home News Feed (s02), which is core to the application's loop.
Maps to SIM-RWD; however, element IDs listed in the 'economy' section (e42, e47, etc.) were flagged as not found in the digest.
Uses the app's 'Home News Feed' and 'AOL' branding, though relies on referencing element IDs that are not present in the digest.
Includes a 3 per day limit and 60-minute cooldown.
Includes a primary metric, guardrails, and a planned 28-day user-level holdout.

requiredChanges: Fix element ID references in the proposal to match the provided product model digest; current references (e42, e47, etc.) were marked as non-existent.
Specify that the 'No thanks' action suppresses the offer for the duration of the current session or until a new trigger boundary to prevent nagging.
